fields.description:
## Context / Problem
A single Gerrit Verified run needs 21 concurrent job slots. The navapbc org is on GitHub Free: 20 total concurrent jobs and 5 concurrent macOS, enforced PER ORGANIZATION and shared with every other navapbc repo. So one run, in an otherwise idle org, cannot fully parallelize; under a 6-change burst later runs queued 6.7-8.4m for a macOS slot, which is what turns a ~21m run into the 41-47m seen from Gerrit.

`.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` contributes 8 of those 21 jobs, each doing 0.4-0.8m of real work while holding a slot for a full checkout + setup-python + install.

## Approach
Two independent reductions, neither weakening the optionality contract.

### 1. Delete the `import-linter` job, and REPAY the guard it provided
It installs `-e .[dev]` (byte-identical to `_build-and-test.yml:230`) and runs `pytest tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py tests/unit/test_optional.py`. Those files carry NO markers, and tests/conftest.py only auto-marks `external` under `tests/external/`, so all 9 tests already run in all four `test` matrix cells (3.11/3.12/3.13 + macOS) — strictly more coverage than the deleted job's single ubuntu/3.12.

The "import-leak test defeated by a polluted process" concern does NOT apply: `test_lean_workflow_runtime_pulls_no_heavy_stack` reads `sys.modules` inside a FRESHLY SPAWNED `subprocess.run([sys.executable,...])`; `test_no_core_module_imports_heavy_stack_at_module_scope` is a pure `ast.parse` walk; `test_blocked_extra_degrades_friendly` uses the `block_extra` fixture which EVICTS modules from `sys.modules` (stronger in a polluted worker); and there is no `COVERAGE_PROCESS_START`/`sitecustomize` in the repo, so even the coverage lane's child is a bare interpreter.

CRITICAL GAP THIS OPENS: nothing in the repo can see the deletion. `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:131-162` asserts only caller-level WIRING strings, and `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py:44-51` reads only caller job keys — neither has visibility into `_optionality.yml`'s inner jobs. After the deletion the ONLY thing keeping those 9 tests running is the incidental absence of a marker; a future contributor adding `@pytest.mark.integration`, or moving the files, deletes the coverage with a GREEN build. So the deletion MUST be paid for with a durable collection guard.

### 2. Collapse the 5 `per-extra` cells + `union` into ONE job, six venv iterations
Five ISOLATION iterations (agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding), each installing ONLY `.[<extra>]` into its own fresh venv; plus one UNION iteration installing `.[agents,eval,tracing]` TOGETHER into a single venv. The union is not redundant: it is the only thing exercising JOINT dependency resolution and can surface a `ResolutionImpossible` no single-extra install can.

Each isolation iteration must reproduce ALL current per-cell work, not just the install:
- `import rebar` with the extra present;
- for extras in `_optional.EXTRAS`, assert `_optional.extra_installed(extra)` (the detection probe);
- `rebar-mcp --help` for the mcp iteration ONLY, reproducing today's `if: matrix.extra == 'mcp'`. Running it everywhere fails in venvs lacking the entry point; dropping it silently weakens the mcp boot check.

TWO ABSOLUTE IMPLEMENTATION RULES, each guarding a silent-failure mode:
- NEVER `source .../activate`. Activations STACK across loop iterations, so PATH decides which interpreter runs and every iteration can silently re-test extra #1.
- ALWAYS invoke by absolute path (`"$v/bin/python"`, `"$v/bin/rebar-mcp"`). A bare `python`/`rebar-mcp` runs the AMBIENT interpreter and can pass while testing nothing. Today's `rebar-mcp --help` (_optionality.yml:178-180) is exactly such a bare console-script call and must be rewritten.

Error isolation is explicit because Actions runs `run:` under `bash -e`: a naive loop dies on the first failure (losing today's `fail-fast: false` diagnostics), while `|| true`/`set +e` without aggregation makes the whole contract a no-op that always passes. Use an `rc` accumulator: guard each iteration with `|| { rc=1; echo "::error::<extra> failed"; continue; }` and end with `exit $rc`.

Venv hygiene: `python -m venv` from a `setup-python` interpreter is already clean (user site-packages disabled, `include-system-site-packages=false`), and `PYTHONPATH`/`PIP_*` are unset in both workflows, so `--copies`/`PYTHONNOUSERSITE`/`--without-pip` are NOT needed. The pip HTTP cache shared across venvs is a speed benefit only (wheels are content-addressed). Do run `pip install --upgrade pip` per venv (ensurepip ships an old pip).

KEEP `clean-core-wheel` byte-identical. It is the check this file's header credits with catching "the module-scope-import class that escaped once", it builds a real wheel, and it is the ONLY lane where `agents_extra_installed()` is False — which is what makes its skipif-degradation tests actually execute.

Rejected: sequential `pip install .[agents]` then `.[eval]` into one shared python — after the first install the env is contaminated, so a missing dependency declaration in a later extra PASSES silently. Rejected: per-extra venvs with no union iteration (loses joint resolution). Rejected: collapsing `clean-core-wheel` too. Considered and not chosen: `strategy: {max-parallel: 1}` on the existing matrix (5->1 peak slots with zero new bash) — the loop was chosen deliberately for the larger slot saving.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` — remove `import-linter`; replace the `per-extra` matrix and `union` jobs with the six-iteration venv-loop job.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` — NEW durable guards (below).
- `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json` — it hard-codes the five doomed check names. It is not the live ruleset (that is Terraform `gerrit-mirror-lock-main`, which has no `required_status_checks`), but it IS POSTed back by `infra/github/rollback-mirror-lock.sh:75-88`, so leaving it stale means an emergency rollback would require checks that cannot exist and freeze `main`.

NOT in scope: `clean-core-wheel`, `_build-and-test.yml`, `gerrit-verify.yaml`.

## Testing
Durable, checked-in guards — not one-time manual observations — so the protection survives the merge:
- assert `tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py` and `tests/unit/test_optional.py` are collected under `-m "not integration and not external"` and yield 9 items (repays the deleted job);
- assert the loop step text contains the `rc` accumulator shape (`continue` and `exit $rc`) and contains NO `activate`, so a later edit cannot reintroduce the swallowed-failure or stacked-activation footguns;
- assert every extra in `_optional.EXTRAS` appears in the looped extra list, so a newly declared extra cannot ship with zero CI (today `metrics` is in `_optional.EXTRAS` with no per-extra coverage, and `pyproject.toml` declares eleven extras against the five covered).

Workflow-level validation: `optionality.yml` triggers on `push`, so pushing a scratch branch to the GitHub mirror exercises the modified reusable end-to-end. A PULL REQUEST does NOT work — `.github/workflows/lockdown.yml` runs `dessant/repo-lockdown` on `pull_request_target` with `close-pr: true` (dependabot exempt), so the mirror auto-closes PRs. `workflow_dispatch` on `optionality.yml` is the fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each of the five extras installs into its own freshly-created venv, never one that already had another extra.
- [ ] A sixth UNION iteration installs `.[agents,eval,tracing]` jointly into one venv.
- [ ] Each isolation iteration runs `import rebar` and, for extras in `_optional.EXTRAS`, asserts `_optional.extra_installed(extra)`.
- [ ] `rebar-mcp --help` runs for the mcp iteration only, invoked by absolute venv path.
- [ ] Every interpreter/console-script call in the loop uses an absolute `"$v/bin/..."` path; the loop contains no `activate`.
- [ ] The loop uses an `rc` accumulator with `continue`, and exits non-zero if any iteration failed.
- [ ] A checked-in test asserts the two optionality test files collect 9 items under the default suite selection.
- [ ] A checked-in test asserts the loop step contains `exit $rc`/`continue` and no `activate`.
- [ ] A checked-in test asserts the looped extra list covers every key in `_optional.EXTRAS`.
- [ ] `clean-core-wheel` is byte-identical to its current form.
- [ ] `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json` no longer names removed checks.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` passes.
- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` passes.
- [ ] `make lint` passes (actionlint covers all workflows).
